final_candidates.decision_summary: N300 sits in the N300-N301-T302 glycan sequon at the V3 base; removing this glycan is a classic escape route from glycan-dependent bNAbs (N301/N332 supersite) with modest expected fitness cost.
N301 is the central glycan attachment site of the supersite; N-to-Q removes the glycan while keeping a similar-sized polar residue, likely minimizing folding/fitness penalty relative to N300D.
G311 lies at the V3 crown GPG tip, a well-known escape determinant for V3-crown antibodies; some fitness risk at the conserved tip keeps confidence moderate.

stop_reason.detail: Pool converged under LLM-only self-review; additional rounds without evidence tools would not improve the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: N300 sits in the N299-N300-N301 stretch at the V3 base and forms a glycan sequon (N300-N301-T302); removing this glycan is a classic escape route from glycan-dependent bNAbs (N301/N332-supersite class). Surface-exposed, single-residue change with modest expected fitness cost.
Glycan sequon removal at the V3 base (N300-N301-T302) is a well-established escape route from glycan-dependent bNAbs with modest fitness cost; remains top candidate.

G311 is in the V3 crown tip (I308-G309-P310-G311-Q312); substitutions at the GPG-tip are well-known escape routes from V3-crown antibodies. Some fitness risk at the conserved tip, so confidence is moderate.
V3 crown GPG-tip substitution disrupts V3-crown antibody binding; retained despite some fitness risk at the conserved tip.

K304 is a surface-exposed basic residue at the V3 base (N301-T302-R303-K304); charge reversal is a common antibody-escape mechanism at V3-base epitopes, but carries some risk of fitness/folding perturbation.
Charge reversal at a surface-exposed V3-base residue is a plausible escape mechanism; kept at moderate confidence due to potential fitness cost.

N301 in the N300-N301-T302 sequon is itself a key glycan attachment site at the N301/N332 supersite; N-to-Q removes the glycan while keeping a similar-sized polar residue, likely lowering folding/fitness penalty relative to N300D. It complements N300D as an alternative sequon-disruption strategy.
